title: Nostr reach. Independent LicoArc core.
summary: Connect to the Nostr network without making it the authority for identity, storage or the lifetime of work.

Independent LicoArc core. Connect to the Nostr network without making it the authority for identity, storage or the lifetime of work. V1 / Generation 1 — Candidate, PARTIAL. This revision changes the security transcript. Formal proof requalification is required; new-session eligibility is false and the Protocol Line is publication ineligible. Standard Nostr messaging remains a separate upstream contract. Definition tests do not establish deployed client support. Two paths, neither a client-brand gate Standard private messaging follows NIP-17, NIP-44 v2 and NIP-59 over NIP-01. Enhanced peers additionally implement the open binding and Endpoint core. An enhanced-only service need not implement a chat interface. Neither path requires LicoUp or official federation membership. Ordinary Nostr messages stay ordinary The standard path keeps kind 14 rumors, kind 13 seals, kind 1059 gift wraps and authenticated kind 10050 recipient inbox lists. NIP-42 is used when the selected relay requires it. Do not put executable commands in chat or infer a sender from a random wrapper key. Bind identity once; update capabilities continuously The experimental, upstream-unallocated inner kind 44900 and exact licoarc.v1 namespace identify enhanced objects. Identity binding names a stable conversation separately from the transport session. Live capability records are protected updates, not frozen binding fields. Invoke/provide roles, availability and execution permission are distinct. Updates reach authorized existing conversations without rebinding or reconnecting; offline peers catch up using durable records and paged snapshots. Preserve protection while changing routes An enhanced operation must never silently become ordinary chat, plaintext or a weaker compatibility copy. Switching an authorized carrier with the same recipient and protection is not a downgrade. Pending pairing has no fixed lifetime; temporary processing limits pause work rather than expire it. A later transport attempt may refresh the outer envelope while preserving the same protected intent and task identity. Nostr is optional, not the communication authority The Endpoint core has five required capabilities. Group collaboration, native HTTPS transport and federation governance have separate targets. Core work remains valid with Nostr disabled. Relay retention and reachability are service properties, not a promise that any public relay stores everything forever. Timestamp-only synchronization is insufficient for arbitrarily late uploads; pending identities and missing data need reconciliation. Definition evidence, not runtime qualification The framing, association, capability and recovery tests are not production cryptography or a real-client interoperability result. The revised native security model is PARTIAL pending proof requalification, so the enhanced adapter must honor the disabled native session-admission gate. It cannot enable the new security profile merely because its own binding is specified. NIP-44 itself does not supply forward secrecy, post-compromise recovery or post-quantum protection. Definition tests do not establish deployed client support. Preserved primitive construction The Candidate retains paired X25519 and ML-KEM-768 one-time prekeys, Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65 authentication, and the X25519 Double Ratchet construction. This is a definition, not a claim that a deployed composite has been audited. Active authorization, not calendar expiry The revised prekey record has no validFrom or validUntil field and no seven-day age rule. Each pair must be genuinely issued, still active under accepted authority, correctly signed and atomically consumed only once. Unresolved asynchronous exchanges retain the material they need; a relay cannot manufacture a prekey or declare one safe. New transcript, explicit requalification Removing signed fields changes transcript identities even though V1 remains V1. Prior proofs and vectors remain inspectable as superseded evidence; they are not rebound to the new bytes. A new positive dual-signature first-packet vector and formal analysis of delayed active-prekey admission remain required. Recover delays without weakening replay protection Ciphertext may arrive far ahead of earlier records. Working limits on skipped-key derivation remain, but a valid pending message is retained and missing history is recovered rather than assigned a message lifetime. Atomic receive persistence preserves authenticated payload and replay state together. Key deletion must not strand the only authorized copy needed by unresolved work. Application-neutral messages The six core classes remain event, request, response, error, cancel and streamChunk. Typed application definitions supply meaning. Protected live capability records update only authorized audiences, with separate invoke/provide roles, availability and execution permission; tools can change in an existing conversation without rebinding. Resumable attachments without an age limit An accepted attachment declaration and its incomplete chunks remain recoverable after the user returns. The old one-day recovery deadline is removed. The existing bounded attachment grammar remains; no unlimited file-size claim is made. Declared digests, chunk validation and explicit storage quotas still apply. Durable intent outlives an attempt Connection failure, a processing budget or a route change may pause delivery, not terminate the accepted request. Persist before acknowledging custody. Retransmission preserves logical identity; safe reprotection on a new session does not create another execution authorization. Receiving and storing a request does not require prior tool-execution approval. Record facts in any network order An authenticated completion can arrive before an acceptance notice. The same result over a new authenticated session remains the same fact. Identical repeats are coalesced instead of building unbounded confirmation history. Conflicting authenticated evidence is retained and stops automatic execution decisions. Missing evidence is unknown, not proof of failure. Cancellation is a request, not a time machine Retain the cancellation intent and the executor’s confirmed outcome separately. A late completion may describe work already performed; recording it must not restart the task. Unknown external effects require inquiry or explicit reconciliation rather than blind retries on another Agent. Recover durable responsibility Recover inbox, outbox, identity and deduplication state before processing. A delivery copy to another device is not another execution assignment. Accepted records and deduplication guards are not disposable UI caches; delete or compact them only after the declared settlement and recovery conditions are met. Formal proof requalification is required; new-session eligibility is false and the Protocol Line is publication ineligible. Standard Nostr messaging remains a separate upstream contract. Definition tests do not establish deployed client support. An independent native carrier The HTTPS Station target retains HTTP/2 and TLS 1.3 framing. Its transport security is not an Endpoint trust decision. Applications can use at least one authorized independent carrier without installing Nostr or federation governance. Five transport operations AFFILIATE, RESERVE, SUBMIT, CLAIM and SETTLE keep distinct purposes. A successful custody admission follows recoverable persistence. A claim temporarily assigns a worker; settling completes or releases the claimed items according to the protected delivery contract. Custody is not Endpoint acceptance A Station receipt never proves that the recipient has durably received, read, approved or executed anything. The sender and any authorized custodians retain responsibility until the contract allows release or verified transfer; no transport hint alone upgrades application finality. Lease expiry releases occupancy, not the message The one-hour storage lifetime and five-minute idempotency expiry are removed. The 300-second claim lease remains only to release a stalled worker’s occupancy. Pending items and duplicate guards survive it. Reject or backpressure new submissions before promising storage when quota is full; do not age-evict accepted undelivered messages. Group Collaboration Each protected Group has Endpoint membership and authenticated state transitions. The existing bounded fan-out construction remains a specific group target, not a limit on every application or every conversation. Historical receipt is not current permission A delayed message can be assessed against authenticated historical membership. Its delivery order does not by itself invalidate it or authorize a new effect. Missing predecessors are fetched; unresolved forks quarantine affected decisions. Revoked devices cannot regain current execution rights by claiming an old date or state. A fork needs a verifiable recovery rule The new resolution record names the uncontested predecessor, the competing changes and one proposed successor. The current construction requires matching votes from every authority in that predecessor. Relay arrival order and an unapproved reduced quorum cannot select a winner. This deliberately does not promise progress when a required authority is permanently unavailable. Federation Governance Federation is a separate network-governance target. Membership, compatibility and abuse signals do not establish local Endpoint trust or grant tool permissions. Roots and roles have limited scope A governance decision is authenticated under its own declared authority rules. It cannot rewrite a user’s conversation, discard pending work or replace the Endpoint’s final admission decision. Copies, users and executors remain distinct Per-device delivery reports remain useful transport facts. They are not automatically equivalent to a person having read a message or every device being allowed to run the same task. Applications declare the intended delivery and execution target.
